title: Preclinical model of type 1 diabetes and myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury in conscious rabbits—demonstration of cardioprotection with rapamycin
protocol: Fasted rabbits for 12 hours before the procedure and supplemented with drinking water.
Sedate rabbits intramuscularly in Biceps femoris muscle using Ketamine (35 mg/kg), Xylazine (5 mg/kg) and Atropine (5 mg/kg).
Dissolve Alloxan monohydrate in sterile saline to prepare a solution of 10 mL at 50 mg/mL.
Keep the prepared Alloxan solution on ice until use.
Aspire the prepared solution into a 10 cc syringe.
Load the syringe onto a microprocessor multiple syringe infusion/withdrawal pump unit (Harvard apparatus, Model series ‘22’ Infuse/withdraw).
Connect the syringe to a standard 6-inch bore extension tube with pinch clamp.
Clean the ear of the rabbit with sterile alcohol pads.
Cannulate the marginal ear vein with a 24G X ¾ inch Safelet IV catheter.
Secure the cannulation by taping to the earlobe using surgical tape.
Adjust the infusion flow rate through the pump to deliver alloxan monohydrate slowly over 10 minutes.
Calculate the volume of alloxan required based on the rabbit's body weight (e.g., 400 mg for a 3.2 kg rabbit).
Administer the calculated volume of alloxan at an average flow rate of 0.8 mL/min through the pump.
Transfer the animal to a recovery cage after administration.
Monitor blood glucose levels using a Contour glucose meter at 1, 2, 3, and 4 hours post-injection.
Use a 26G X 3/8 needle to pierce the small vein in the earlobe for blood sugar measurement.
Supplement with 5% dextrose (10 mL, i.m.) if the blood glucose level drops below 70 mg/dL.
Continue monitoring and supplementing as necessary until at least 4 hours post-alloxan administration.
Transport animals back to the vivarium after 4 hours of alloxan treatment.
Provide normal food and 20% glucose in drinking water for the next 3 days.
Check the health and blood sugar levels of animals 10-12 hours after alloxan administration.
Administer 5% dextrose intramuscularly if blood sugar level drops below 70 mg/dL.
Measure blood glucose twice daily (morning/evening) for four weeks in maintained rabbits.
Inject insulin intramuscularly when blood glucose exceeds 450 mg/dL based on dosage guidelines provided.
Anesthetize the rabbits by administering ketamine, Xylazine, and Atropine intramuscularly.
Shave the appropriate surgical area from the sternum to left shoulder blade of rabbits using a handheld vacuum-assisted hair removal system.
Intubate the rabbits with an endotracheal tube for mechanical ventilation.
Ventilate the rabbits with oxygen-enriched air at 28-30 breaths per minute.
Intubate rabbits with an endotracheal tube for mechanical ventilation.
Apply Betadine to the surgical area with sterile gauze and allow it to dry.
Administer Buprenorphine SR LAB (0.1 mg/kg, i.m.) before surgery.
Provide Gentamicin (0.7 mg/kg; i.m.; each day) prior to surgery and on the first and second postoperative days.
Monitor body temperature continuously with a rectal probe attached to a thermocouple.
Use a heating blanket to maintain body temperature between 36°C–39°C.
Perform a left thoracotomy in the fourth intercostal space under sterile conditions.
Expose the heart by opening the pericardium.
Identify the left anterior descending artery (LAD).
Pass a 4-0 taper-needled silk suture beneath a major branch of the LAD, perpendicular to the vessel.
Place a balloon occluder using Tygon tubing on the coronary artery.
Secure the balloon occluder with a 4-0 silk suture on the anterior left ventricular wall.
Inflate the balloon briefly (10 seconds) and check for cyanosis of distal myocardium.
Deflate the balloon and confirm hyperemia in the myocardium.
Use an Ambu bag to inflate the lungs.
Close the pericardium using 4-0 silk suture.
Close the rib using 0 Perma-HandTM silk suture.
Close muscle and skin with 3-0 monofilament suture, leaving a small incision for catheter retrieval.
Tunnel the occluder tubing under the skin.
Exteriorize the tubing through a small incision between the scapulae.
Place a sterile chest tube prior to closing the chest to remove fluid and air.
Apply triple-antibiotic (Neosporin) ointment after surgery.
Extubate rabbit when they show eyeball movement in response to light and diaphragm movement for abdominal breathing.
Transfer rabbit to recovery unit once extubated.
Monitor rabbit continuously until fully awake.
Take necessary measurements to ensure animals cannot access or pull the catheter at the exit site.
Minimize incision size between shoulder blades.
Periodically monitor animals closely, at least twice a day.
Use protective neck collar to make it less accessible.
Sedate rabbits to avoid confounding effects of anesthetics and postsurgical complications.
Clean the ear with sterile ethanol pads.
Establish venous line by placing a 24-gauge angiocatheter on a marginal ear vein for blood sampling and drug administration.
Cannulate the ear dorsal artery under local anesthesia (Lidocaine Hydrochloride Jelly USP, 2%) to monitor arterial pressure.
Under sedation, inflate the hydraulic balloon occluder to induce a 45-minute coronary artery occlusion.
Monitor vital cardiac parameters including mean arterial pressure, systolic pressure, diastolic pressure, and heart rate throughout the procedure.
Deflate the hydraulic balloon after 45 minutes of ischemia to allow reperfusion for 3 days.
Collect blood samples (0.5 mL) in heparinized tubes at baseline and at 1, 2, 4, and 24 hours post-reperfusion.
Centrifuge the blood sample at 2000g for 10 minutes under refrigerated conditions (4°C).
Separate plasma from the centrifuged blood sample.
Store the separated plasma at -20°C to measure cardiac troponin (cTnI).
Transfer the rabbit to the recovery unit and continuously monitor until it awakens.
Monitor the rabbit closely to ensure adequate breathing and prevent hypothermia and dehydration.
Intubate and mechanically ventilate with oxygen-enriched air if severe breathing problems occur.
Check for symptoms of dehydration such as sticky saliva, crusty eyes, or dark urine after surgery.
Inject saline (5 mL/h) intravenously during surgery and post-operative recovery to avoid dehydration and compensate for blood loss/withdrawal.
Provide unrestricted drinking water in the recovery chamber and vivarium.
Transport the rabbit back to the vivarium with normal food and drinking water when it can stand on its legs without imbalance.
Infuse Rapamycin (0.25 mg/kg) slowly intravenously through the marginal ear vein for 10 minutes, 5 minutes before reperfusion begins in sedated rabbits undergoing 45 minutes of ischemia.
Assess cardiac function by echocardiography at 2 hours post-reperfusion.
Sedate rabbits with inhalation of isoflurane (2.5%).
Place the rabbit on the table in a left lateral recumbent position.
Supply oxygen and isoflurane mixture (4.0%) to sedate the rabbit using a small canine mask.
Adjust the isoflurane concentration (2.5%–3.5%) as needed during echocardiography.
Perform echocardiographic measurements using a Vevo2100TM at various time points.
Conduct ech cardiographic measurements before and after alloxan treatment, after balloon implantation, and 3 days post I/R.
Use the MS201 probe on the parasternal view to measure cardiac function.
Measure left ventricular (LV) function using two-dimensional ultrasound B-Mode (Short Axis).
Record M-Mode data for further analysis of cardiac function.
Remove chest hairs using a handheld vacuum-assisted hair removal system.
Apply hair removal cream/gel to the remaining chest hairs.
Prewarm ultrasound gel.
Apply prewarmed ultrasound gel to the chest overlying the heart.
Centrifuge a 60cc syringe filled with ultrasound gel at 2000g for 10 minutes to remove air bubbles.
Measure cardiac left ventricle (LV) function using two-dimensional ultrasound B-Mode in the Short Axis view and M-Mode in the Parasternal view.
Place the MS201 probe on the chest to access the LV anterior, posterior walls, intraventricular septal wall, and lateral wall.
Measure the diameter of the LV lumen as LV internal diameter (LVID).
Calculate LV ejection fraction (LVEF), LV end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD), end-systolic diameter (LVESD) and stroke volumes (SV) by tracing end- and epicardial borders during contraction.
Analyze obtained images using Vevo LAB 3.2.0 software for infarct size measurement.
Anesthetize rabbits by administering ketamine, Xylazine, and Atropine via intramuscular injection.
Clean the ear with sterile ethanol pads.
Infuse heparin through the ear vein.
Euthanize rabbits using saturated potassium chloride via catheter connected to ear auricular artery.
Excise the heart and mount it through the aortic root on a 60 c.c. syringe.
Perfuse the heart with Krebs-Henseleit buffer at 37°C to remove blood.
Remove the balloon occluder from the coronary artery.
Tie a double knot using a 4-O suture around the coronary artery at the balloon occlusion site.
Infuse phthalo blue dye solution through the aortic root to demarcate risk and non-risk areas.
Cut the heart into 5–6 transverse slices (∼2-mm-thick/slice) using tissue slicer blades.
Stain the heart slices with 1% triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) in phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Fix the stained heart slices in 10% formalin for 4 hours.
Remove atrial and RV (right ventricle) tissues from the fixed heart slices.
Number LV (left ventricle) slices from apex to base as 1 through 5/6.
Photograph both sides of the numbered LV slices with a ruler.
Using Image J software, measure the area of total LV, red region, blue tissue, and white region.
Express the region at risk as a percentage of the LV.
Calculate the infarct as a percentage of the risk area.
Dilute plasma samples 10× with cTnI diluent before measuring cTnI.
Prepare standards of cTnI from the cTnI stock by serial diluting according to kit instructions.
Dispense diluted plasma samples (200 μL) into ELISA plate wells in duplicate.
Incubate the plate for 2 h at 25°C on a plate shaker at 150 rpm.
Discard solutions from the wells of the plate after incubation.
Wash each well five times with 1× wash solution (400 μL/well/each time).
Add 100 μL of diluent to each well.
Add 100 μL of HRP-conjugate to each well.
Incubate the plate at 25°C for one hour on a plate shaker at 150 rpm.
Discard solutions from the wells after incubation.
Wash each well five times with 1× wash solution (400 μL/well/each time).
Remove residual droplets by tapping the plate on clean paper towels.
Dispense 100 μL of TMB into each well.
Incubate the plate at 25°C for 20 min on a plate shaker at 150 rpm.
Add 100 μL of Stop solution to each well after 20 min incubation.
Measure the absorbance at 450 nm using a plate reader within 5 minutes.
Prepare a standard curve by plotting absorbance values against log10 of concentration.
Dissect the risk area of the LV after 72 h of reperfusion and fix in 10% formalin for at least 1 day after washing with PBS.
Prepare 5 μm thick tissue sections from paraffin-embedded samples.
Stain the sections using a Terminal Deoxynucleotidyl Transferase dUTP Nick end Labeling (TUNEL) kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Deparaffinize the tissue sections using xylene.
Dehydrate the sections with 96%, 90%, and 80% ethanol concentrations.
Rehydrate the sections in distilled water.
Microwave the slides containing tissue sections in 1× Citrate Buffer at high power for 10 minutes.
Allow the slides to cool slowly to a temperature range of 20°C–22°C.
Incubate the tissue sections with equilibration buffer, nucleotide mix, and TdT enzyme under dark conditions at 37°C for 1 hour.
Wash the slides with PBS three times, each wash lasting 5 minutes.
Incubate the tissue sections with 5% normal goat serum at a temperature range of 20°C–22°C for 1 hour.
Incubate the tissue sections overnight at 4°C with troponin antibody (mouse Troponin T).
Wash the slides with PBS three times, each wash lasting 5 minutes.
Incubate the tissue sections with anti-mouse IgG (Alexa Fluor® 594 Conjugate) for further analysis.
Fix the tissue sections with DAPI anti-fade mount solution.
Count apoptotic cells with green nuclei under a fluorescence microscope.
Count total cells with DAPI-blue nuclei under a fluorescence microscope.
Plot the data as the percentage of apoptotic cells to total cells.
Confirm cardiomyocyte apoptosis in myocardium by co-localization of green nuclei with troponin staining in red striated cells.
